frozen_authority.quarantine_note: A main-ref discovery response included unrelated transport metadata. It was quarantined and not used as semantic evidence.

slice.question: Can a repository-only protocol admit immutable generation-tagged effects without a protected shared fence, while preventing stale-generation admission across handoff crashes and replays?
slice.selection_reason: Exact latest own-state continuation; direct zero-cost architecture before further decomposition.

architecture.prepared_record: Create an immutable candidate record containing effect payload hash, actor, owner generation, and the exact predecessor HEAD identity. Creation alone is PREPARED and never counts as an accepted effect.
architecture.canonical_head: Maintain one CAS-guarded mutable HEAD containing current owner, generation, sequence/revision, and committed record tip.
architecture.effect_commit: Accept an effect only when a CAS from the exact predecessor HEAD succeeds and the candidate actor/generation matches the predecessor owner/generation.
architecture.handoff_commit: Represent ownership transfer as another immutable record whose single HEAD CAS simultaneously advances owner/generation and the canonical tip.
architecture.validation: A repository-visible effect is accepted only if its immutable record is on the canonical committed HEAD chain and its predecessor/actor/generation transition validates. Orphan prepared records are visible data but not effects.
architecture.crash_rule: A crash before HEAD CAS leaves only an orphan PREPARED record. A crash after HEAD CAS may lose local acknowledgement but not canonical state; later exact readback can rediscover the committed tip.
architecture.replay_rule: Duplicate replay of the same committed record is idempotent when it is still the tip; after any later HEAD advance, its stale predecessor CAS cannot revert or re-admit it.

finite_model.safety_property: Every accepted effect record's actor/generation equals the owner/generation of its exact predecessor canonical HEAD.
finite_model.race_result: Effect-commit and handoff-commit prepared from the same predecessor cannot both win; the first successful HEAD CAS invalidates the other's predecessor.
finite_model.replay_result: No replay path in the enumerated model reverted owner generation or accepted an effect from a stale predecessor.

finding.key_reason: The only admission point is one mutable CAS root. Immutable record creation is non-effectful preparation, so owner advancement and effect admission are not two independently accepted mutable writes.
finding.availability_tradeoff: A lost acknowledgement after successful HEAD CAS creates temporary local uncertainty, not stale-effect admission; recovery requires later HEAD readback.
finding.generalization_limit: This proves only the modeled repository-visible effect class. It does not make an arbitrary non-repository external side effect conditional on repository CAS/readback and does not establish cross-service atomicity.

tested_scope.kind: finite state-model property check plus repository-transport architecture

phase1_acceptance.global_residual_dependency: Mapping arbitrary non-repository externally visible effects into this repository-native commit model remains unresolved; no protected/manual/richer executor is accepted as a substitute.
phase1_acceptance.quota_note: Only lightweight repository transport is assumed; it is not used as compute and rate-limit interruption must be handled by checkpoint/resume across invocations.
phase1_acceptance.conflict_check: Only frozen sanitized controls, own role-local state, and role-local finite reasoning were used semantically. No O/O-derived, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, commit-message/diff, or unrelated transport semantics were used.

continuation.exact_next_action: Fresh-bootstrap the required controls, exact-read reasoning LATEST/checkpoint, then execute exactly one bounded lost-ack leaf: model a successful canonical HEAD CAS whose response is not observed before crash, and test whether next-invocation readback plus exact record identity can distinguish (a) commit landed and is still tip, (b) commit landed but a later authorized HEAD advance occurred, and (c) commit never landed, without duplicate effect admission or owner rollback. If the repository-only recovery is safe, persist that result while keeping arbitrary non-repository external effects as an unresolved child; if unsafe, persist the minimal counterexample. Do not start the separate outcome-classification leaf in the same invocation.
